solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One who fails to turn up food bowl centrally

definitions.text: One who fails to turn up

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the inner letters are kept

blocks.note: nosh is informal British slang for food
the two middle letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone who never arrives, while their bowl of food waits on the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' sounds like a reversal signal, but it belongs to the definition: a person who fails to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-show is the standard noun for a person who books or promises to attend and then never appears.

clue.text: Pet above a river — German one

definitions.note: 'one' stands for a river, picking up the word just before it

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece placed above another comes first in the grid

blocks.note: to neck is to kiss and cuddle, as is to pet
taken as written
R is the standard abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A pet animal perched above a river, apparently a German one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pet' looks like a noun for an animal, but it is the verb: to pet is to neck. 'German one' leans on 'river' to mean a German river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neckar is a major tributary of the Rhine flowing through Stuttgart and Heidelberg in southwest Germany.

clue.text: Premier having drink with army engineers

indicators.note: being accompanied means sitting alongside, so the parts simply join up

blocks.note: to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers of the British Army

explanation.surface: A prime minister having a drink with soldiers from an engineering corps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Premier' reads as a noun, the head of government, but it is the adjective meaning foremost. RE is the usual army engineers; here it is the longer REME.
explanation.definitionFit: Premier as an adjective means first in rank or highest in importance, the same idea as top or chief.

clue.text: In Australia, you no longer can make public call

indicators.note: to be within a place is to be enclosed by it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: Oz is the informal name for Australia
ye is the archaic plural form of you, no longer used

explanation.surface: Someone in Australia complaining that a public telephone call is no longer possible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In Australia' reads as a setting, but it places one piece inside the country's nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Oyez is the cry used by a town crier or court officer to demand silence and attention before an announcement.

clue.text: Jack meets Elizabeth, religious woman

indicators.note: two things that meet end up side by side, so they join

blocks.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an AB, an able seaman
Bess is a short form of the name

explanation.surface: A man called Jack meets a woman called Elizabeth, who turns out to be devout.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack and Elizabeth look like two people; Jack is a sailor (jack tar), and Elizabeth is shortened to a pet name.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbess is the female head of a convent of nuns, so she is a woman in religious orders.

clue.text: One in local posh hotel somewhere in southwest France

indicators.note: being inside a place means being enclosed by it

blocks.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub, here a bar
the Roman numeral for one
the Ritz is a famously luxurious London hotel

explanation.surface: A tourist in a smart local hotel somewhere in the south of France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' is British slang for the pub nearest your home, here giving a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Biarritz is a seaside resort town on the Bay of Biscay coast near the Spanish border.

clue.text: Standoffish, Republican failing to stress feelings

indicators.note: something that fails is absent, so that letter drops out

blocks.note: a remote person is distant and aloof
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An aloof Republican politician who cannot manage to show emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R from the front of REMOTE leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To emote is to display emotion in an exaggerated, theatrical way, as an actor overplaying a scene does.

clue.text: During day, iron’s most secure

indicators.note: what happens during a period is held within it

blocks.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron, plus the S of the apostrophe

explanation.surface: Ironing clothes in daytime is the most secure way to do it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'iron's' supplies a letter, not just a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Safe means protected from danger; its superlative describes the place or option with the least risk.

clue.text: Tree canopy peripherally attracts crowd

indicators.note: the periphery is the edge, so only the outside letters are kept

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the word
a press is a crowd pushing together, as in the press of people

explanation.surface: A shady tree whose canopy draws a crowd of people underneath it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canopy' sounds like part of the tree, but only its outer two letters are used.
explanation.definitionFit: The cypress is a coniferous evergreen, often tall and slender, common in Mediterranean landscapes and graveyards.

clue.text: Huge number of calamari briefly overwhelming large cat

indicators.note: made brief means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
in a down entry, to overwhelm is to sit over the top, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: calamari is squid served as food
L is the abbreviation for large
a lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: An enormous quantity of squid rings piled on top of a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: SQUID loses its D. 'Huge number of' could be read as the start of the wordplay; the definition stops at 'number'.
explanation.definitionFit: Squillion is jokey informal slang for an unspecified, enormous quantity, like zillion or gazillion.

clue.text: A backward idiot, reserved and haughty

indicators.note: going backward means reading from the end to the start

blocks.note: taken as written
a fool is an idiot

explanation.surface: A dim-witted person who is also stuck-up and cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' reads as an insult alongside 'idiot', but it tells you to reverse the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aloof keeps their distance and seems cool and superior, unfriendly toward others.

clue.text: Training unknown on top-grade peak

indicators.note: placed after something, so this pair follows the first piece

blocks.note: A is the top grade in exams
PE is physical education
x is the classic unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: Mountaineering practice on an unknown, top-class summit.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue, 'on' puts the training and unknown after the top grade.
explanation.definitionFit: An apex is the highest point or tip of something, such as a mountain summit.

clue.text: Two pints, then European residents vacated lodging

indicators.note: a vacated building has its contents cleared out, leaving only the shell

blocks.note: a quart is two pints
E is the abbreviation for European
first and last letters, with the inside removed

explanation.surface: After a couple of pints, some European tenants moved out of their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vacated' means emptied: only the first and last letters of 'residents' remain.
explanation.definitionFit: Quarters are rooms or accommodation where someone lives or is stationed, as in soldiers' quarters.

clue.text: Illness universal in winter month — daughter itches regularly

indicators.note: being inside something means it surrounds you
at regular intervals means every other letter is taken

blocks.note: Jan is the abbreviation for January
U is the film certificate for universal viewing
D is the abbreviation for daughter
the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A sickness going round in January, with a daughter itching all over.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film rating for universal viewing.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice is a medical condition, usually from liver trouble, that turns the skin and eyes yellow.

clue.text: Clothing adornment, gold, hired out through Pete at work

indicators.note: something at work is busy moving about, so its letters get rearranged
running through something means passing inside it, so it is enclosed

blocks.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
to let a property is to hire it out
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Pete wears a uniform with gold trim, a hired costume, to his job.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pieces sit together inside the rearranged name, splitting it after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An epaulette is an ornamental shoulder piece on a coat or military uniform jacket.

clue.text: Broadcast live, Sue is difficult to understand

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter widely, as seed is sown, so the letters are spread into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A presenter named Sue on a live programme who makes no sense to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast live' reads as radio jargon, but 'Broadcast' scatters the letters of 'live' and 'Sue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Elusive describes something hard to grasp or pin down, whether an idea or a meaning.

clue.text: Quartet carrying Authorised Version showing goodwill

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: a quartet is a group of four
the initials A and V of Authorised Version, the King James Bible

explanation.surface: A singing quartet carrying a Bible and spreading kindness.
explanation.walkthrough: AV is the standard abbreviation for the 1611 English Bible translation.
explanation.definitionFit: Favour means approval, kindness or friendly support toward someone, which is goodwill.

clue.text: Dash hopefully on the outside, with horse in enclosure

indicators.note: only the exterior of the word counts, its two ends
something inside a space is surrounded by it

blocks.note: first and last letters
a pen is a fenced enclosure for animals
H is slang for heroin, which is also called horse

explanation.surface: Hoping to make a dash on the outside track, with a horse in the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dash' and 'horse' suggest racing; horse is slang for heroin, which is H.
explanation.definitionFit: A dash and a hyphen are both short horizontal punctuation lines; loosely the terms overlap.

clue.text: Father taken aback by pictures informally covering last supplement

indicators.note: taken back means turned round to face the other way
a cover goes around what it hides, so it encloses it
next to, so the pieces sit beside each other

blocks.note: pa is an informal word for father
pix is informal shorthand for pictures
the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Dad is shocked by some snapshots in the final pages of a magazine supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taken aback' reads as surprised, but it means turned back.
explanation.definitionFit: An appendix is supplementary material added at the end of a book or report.

clue.text: Quietly managed to consume whiskey and seafood

indicators.note: consuming means taking inside, so one piece swallows the other

blocks.note: p is piano, the musical direction to play quietly
to run a business is to manage it
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Someone quietly got through a glass of whiskey and a plate of seafood.
explanation.walkthrough: Whiskey, spelt with an E, is the radio code word for W.
explanation.definitionFit: A prawn is a small edible shellfish, a common example of seafood.

clue.text: Heard of crucial landing-place

indicators.note: something heard is taken in by ear, so the sound matters rather than the spelling

blocks.note: key as an adjective means crucial, as in a key point

explanation.surface: Being told about an important place for boats to land.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words are pronounced 'kee' in British English.
explanation.definitionFit: A quay is a stone or concrete platform along a harbour where boats moor and unload.

clue.text: Joseph grasping king’s quip

indicators.note: to grasp is to hold tightly, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: Joe is the short form of the name
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A man named Joseph catching on to a witty remark made by the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'king's' is just 'is' or possessive glue; only K is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A quip is a short witty remark, which is a kind of jest or funny line.

clue.text: Took a picture: that’s capturing large ruminant

indicators.note: a capture holds its prize inside, so the letters sit within the clue words

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling the first three words

explanation.surface: A wildlife photographer who snapped a big grazing animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took a picture' sounds like a definition, snapped or shot, but it is the source text.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a cud-chewing forest mammal of central Africa, the only living relative of the giraffe.

clue.text: Henry follows unusual one burning Stone Age artefact

indicators.note: something unusual is out of the ordinary order, so the letters are rearranged
coming after means placed at the end of the sequence

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
something burning is lit
H is the henry, the SI unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A man called Henry trailing after an odd person who is setting a prehistoric tool alight.
explanation.walkthrough: Henry looks like a person's name but is the physics unit abbreviated H.
explanation.definitionFit: A neolith is a polished stone tool or weapon from the New Stone Age, the Neolithic period.

clue.text: Copy campanologist?

blocks.note: first meaning: a lookalike
second meaning: a person who sounds church bells

explanation.walkthrough: Campanology is the art of bell-ringing; the question mark flags the playful pairing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dead ringer is an exact double of someone, and bell enthusiasts who pull the ropes are called by this word.

clue.text: Each recalled info about a sea between Greece and Turkey

indicators.note: called back means brought back the way it came, so read in the opposite direction
about means around, so one piece goes around another

blocks.note: ea is the abbreviation for each
gen is British slang for information
taken as written

explanation.surface: Everyone remembering facts about a body of water in the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: Gen is British informal slang for information, as in 'get the gen'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aegean is the arm of the Mediterranean lying between mainland Greece and the Anatolian coast.
